note: Macintosh Classic RAM card (garrettsworkshop/MacClassicRAMCard, release-4406A): '3 MB low-profile RAM card'. TWO layers, 68.6x46mm, 26 footprints, 40 nets, 340 vias in the source. Two AS4C1M16F5 EDO DRAMs in SOJ-42 sharing a 16-bit DQ bus and 10 address nets (28-30-net links to a 2x22 socket) plus 9 RAS/CAS nets; a controller-less EDO DRAM board.

Allwinner A13 test SBC (servomouse/A13_test_project): 4 layers, 80x50mm, 149 footprints. An eLQFP-176 SoC (not a BGA) drives an AS4C256M16D3 DDR3 x16 in a 96-ball BGA through a 48-net link -- 16 DQ, 4 DQS, 15 address -- plus a K9GAG08 NAND on a TSOP-48 (8 NAND_IO).

Allwinner H616 (TFBGA-284) development board (Kononenko-K/Allwinner_H616_Devboard, CERN-OHL-P-2.0): 4 layers, 58x66mm, 165 footprints. A whole LPDDR4 SoC board, unlike the Antmicro memory-test boards already in the corpus (lpddr4_testbed, lpddr4_tester): an IS43LQ32256A x32 LPDDR4 in a 200-ball BGA behind a 55-net link -- 32 DQ, 8 DQS (4 differential pairs), 4 DQM. Ships a .kicad_dru of per-netclass skew rules (DDR_ADDR and DDR_DATA_0..3, max 3.175mm). Carries 165 net-tagged copper graphic segments (power-plane art the router cannot target, #513).

Icepi SBC (cheyao/icepi-sbc, Icy Electronics): Allwinner H3 (347-ball 0.65mm BGA) with an H5TQ4G63EFR DDR3 x16 in a 96-ball BGA behind a 50-net link -- 16 DQ, 4 DQS, 2 DQM, 16 address. 4 layers, 85x56mm, 280 footprints, 1428 pads, 54 zones plus eMMC, GPIO and FPC. The densest of the DDR3 SoC boards by part count.

NXP i.MX6ULZ (289-ball 0.8mm BGA) with a K4B4G1646E DDR3L x16 in a 96-ball BGA, 47-net link: 4 layers, 50x50mm, 164 footprints, 36 zones. Ships a .kicad_dru of LENGTH-window rules keyed on netclass (byte0 delay matching on DRAM_LDQ min 11.5 / opt 13 / max 14.5mm; a 100-ohm differential class with a 27.05..31.05mm target) -- length constraints rather than the clearance/width rules the other dru boards carry.

Mackerel-30 prototype (crmaykish/mackerel-68k, MIT): a 68030 single-board computer. 4 layers, 215x150mm, 133 footprints, 1121 pads. PGA-169 MC68030, an EPM7128 CPLD in a PLCC-84 socket and a 72-pin SIMM on 32-bit D and A buses with 16-bit IDE and expansion data buses -- the same CPU family as maxi030 but a different design, layout style and designer.

MAXI030 (aslak3/MAXI030, GPL-2.0): an expandable MC68030 computer. 4 layers, 239x166mm, 222 footprints, 2137 pads, 443 nets -- the largest net count of the set. PGA-128 68030 and a PQFP-240 EPF10K130 FPGA (30-net link) with two 72-pin SIMM sockets on 32-bit SD/D/A buses, a 24-bit expansion address bus and a 16-bit IDE bus. Same designer as set6's mdfpga_hub75; a different design (dedupe 0.067).

Amiga N2630 (jasonsbeer/Amiga-N2630, 'a re-imagining of the Amiga A2630 processor card', Rev 4.1.0a, MC68882 PLCC variant): 4 layers, 318x124.5mm, 248 footprints, 1987 pads, 381 nets, 1769 zones. Two SDRAM chips (TSOP-II-54, 16Mx16 and 4Mx16) behind an XC95144XL CPLD (22-net links) on 32-bit D, EMD and address buses, plus a 16-bit IDE bus -- a long 32-bit bus stack on a big board.

Universal PCIe Gen3 x16 powered active backplane (TeinkBR/pcie-active-backplane, 4-layer variant): 202x160mm, only 47 footprints but 1233 pads and 92 routable nets. A x16 host edge connector feeds a CEM x16 slot through 32 TX and 32 RX nets (a 69-net edge-to-slot link) -- sixteen lanes of differential pairs across a large, sparse board.

Microchip AT91SAM9G25 open SBC module (vd-rd/sbc_at91sam9g25, hw-compute/module): 4 layers, 66x42mm, 111 footprints. A DDR2 board -- a DDR2-x16 in an 84-ball BGA, 44-net link: 16 data, 13 address, 2 DQS, 2 DQM -- beside an 18-bit LCD bus and two pin headers. Ships a .kicad_dru scoped `(layer outer)` and conditioned on `A.insideCourtyard('U1')` / `('U200')` (CPU and DRAM BGA fan-out, track/clearance min 0.1016mm). Same designer as set12's allwinner_a13_som (dedupe 0.239, under the 0.30 bar; a different SoC and a different board, no shared schematic symbols).

Stanlazy's XC7Z010 'ruler' SoM (Stanlazy/ZYNQ_Ruler, LGPL-2.1): 4 layers, an 88x23.4mm strip carrying a CLG400 Zynq and an MT41K256M16 DDR3L (96-ball BGA) on a 49-net link -- 16 DQ, 4 DQS, 15 address, 7 clock nets -- with a 31-pin 1mm header edge. 225 footprints, 1529 pads, 112 zones: an extreme aspect ratio (3.8:1) with a full DDR3 bus in it.

A500/2000 2MEG CHIP RAM pin-header adapter, Rev D (LIV2/A500-2Meg-Chip-ram, LIV2 & Kavanoz): retrofits a 2MB Agnus into a 1MB Amiga. TWO layers, 60.6x44.9mm, only 18 footprints but 90 routable nets: a 72-net Agnus 8375 <-> 8372A link plus a 1Mx16 DRAM (SOJ-42) with a 16-bit DRD bus, 20 address and RAS/CAS nets -- the densest nets-per-footprint board in the set.

A591 (conorOCS/a591, GPL-3.0): 'Compact Flash HDD and 8MB Fast RAM side-port expansion for Amiga 500'. 4 layers, 67x134mm, 75 footprints, 139 nets. An XC9572XL-TQ100 CPLD bridges the A500 side-expansion connector (a 28-net link, 23 address, 16 data) to an IS42S16400J 64Mbit SDRAM (a 20-net link) and a Compact Flash socket.

Amiga A500 DRAM expansion (rlake/AmigaA500DRAM): TWO layers, 57x72mm, 38 footprints, 97 nets. Three 16-bit data buses (XDRD, RDRD and IO), 10 address and 18 RAS/CAS strobes between the Amiga side and the DRAM -- a two-layer DRAM bus board (no controller IC: the bus is the design).

CIDER (LIV2/CIDER, GPL-2.0): 'CDTV IDE + RAM + FlashROM'. 4 layers, 75x57mm, 75 footprints, 161 nets, 624 pads. An XC95144XL-TQ100 CPLD in front of an MT48LC8M16A2P SDRAM (a 22-net link) with 24-bit address and three 16-bit data buses (D, R_D, B_D). Ships a .kicad_dru of the JLCPCB 4-layer rule set (hole_clearance, via and PTH size limits conditioned on Type == 'Via'/'hole').

Computie 68k-SBC rev 2 (transistorfet/computie, GPL-3.0): a 68000 single-board computer on TWO layers, 155x140mm, 78 footprints, 558 pads, 114 nets. 23-bit address and 16-bit data buses plus four clock nets. One board from a repo that ships several (68k-SMT, K30, supervisor shield); the others are not included so the set does not stack near-duplicates.

GottaGoFaZt3r SD (LIV2/GottaGoFaZt3r, CC-BY-SA-4.0): 'Zorro III Fast RAM for Amiga 3000/4000'. 4 layers, 129x53mm, 71 footprints, 159 nets, 666 pads. A Zorro III edge connector (50-net link) into an XC95144XL CPLD with two pairs of AS4C32M16SC SDRAM chips (18-net links) on 32-bit MD and D buses and a 24-bit AD bus.

M68000 single-board computer (jack-mil/mcd-pcb, 'MCD 2022'): TWO layers, 148x71mm, 75 footprints, 116 nets. A PLCC-68 socketed MC68000 and an XC9572 CPLD in a PLCC-84 socket on a 16-bit data / 19-bit address bus (a 21-net CPU-to-CPLD link), all through-hole-ish retro parts; a two-layer bus board.

PiStorm'X 1K2 (f1ac0/PistormX, Amiga 1200 version): a PiStorm CPU-replacement adapter -- an XC95288XL CPLD (TQFP-144) between the A1200 trapdoor/CPU-socket edge connector (FCN-225, a 78-net link) and a Raspberry Pi 2x20 header (28 nets). TWO layers, 76x99mm, only 27 footprints but 435 pads, 125 nets and 493 vias in the source: a 32-bit data / 24-bit address bus escaping from a fine-pitch CPLD on a two-layer board.

RAM2E II, GW4203C (garrettsworkshop/RAM2E, release-GW4203C): RAMWorks-compatible auxiliary RAM for the Apple IIe. 4 layers, 78x50mm, 78 footprints, 124 nets, 1227 zones. An Intel 5M240Z MAX V CPLD (TQFP-100) drives a W9812G6KH-6 128Mbit SDRAM (TSOP-II-54) over a 29-net link with 12 RA, 8 MD, 8 RD and 8 VD nets -- a dense CPLD-plus-SDRAM board.

STM32H7S3 system-on-module (phancak/STM32H7_Board, MIT): 4 layers, 100x50mm, 112 footprints, 800 zones. An LQFP-176 STM32H7S3 shares its FMC bus (16 data, 13 address) between an SDRAM and a NAND (MX30LF1G18AC on TSOP-48), behind a 62-pin Amphenol board-to-board connector (38 BTB nets) -- a parallel memory bus on a 4-layer module without a BGA anywhere.

Commodore 64 ASSY 250407 motherboard replica (bwack/C64-250407-Replica-KiCad v1.3, CERN-OHL-1.2). TWO layers, 390x180mm, 227 footprints, all through-hole except 40 SMD pads on 5 parts (CN2/CN3 edge fingers, JP1, VR1, VR2): 1161 PTH + 16 NPTH pads. 6510 CPU, VIC-II, SID, two CIAs, PLA, ROMs and eight DRAMs on a multi-drop A0-A15/D0-D7 bus (11-12 pads per net), 61 Earth/+5V pour zones. Its routing replicates Commodore's hand-taped artwork (6582 segments, 574 vias): buses horizontal on F.Cu, vertical on B.Cu. Admitted 2026-10-08 as the public stand-in for issue #1219, a 2-layer all-through-hole pinball MPU whose owner reported the router's output as spaghetti. Source artifacts: 8 net-tagged copper graphics on CAN+5V (#513: KiCad reports that net unconnected on every run) and 12 footprints sharing the reference REF** (#726).
